newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - ASDA to bring early Xmas cheer.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - ASDA to bring early Xmas cheer.

text.p: British supermarket sector favourite ASDA Plc is expected to bring fans early Christmas cheer with strong half year results and striding sales growth when it reports on December 19, analysts said.

Pretax profits are likely to rise to between 155 million stg and 161 million stg from 138.3 million stg a year ago with a dividend payout of around 0.85 pence per share, up from 0.72 pence previously.
Analysts said there could be some exceptional charges for provisions.
"It is a selling success story, we should see a very, very good performance," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

ASDA's sales from existing stores, stripping out the impact of new openings and disposals, could show gains of 8.5-10 percent over a year ago, ahead of the 7.5 percent gain reported by market leader Tesco in September, as its focus on quality at cheap prices proves successful, analysts said.
"That is a very robust performance, they are still moving forward and they are managing without a loyalty card," the analyst said.
ASDA has deferred from launching a nationwide loyalty card even though its major competitors -- Tesco, J. Sainsbury and Safeway -- all now offer these to customers.
ASDA has a loyalty card on trial in selected stores but has said it sees no reason to launch one yet as sales momentum continues upward.
The half year results will be the first with Allan Leighton in the role of chief executive, where he moved from the deputy position in September, taking over from the ebullient Archie Norman.

Norman, now standing as a prospective parliamentary candidate for the ruling Conservatives, was renowned for his unorthodox management style, which saw all staff described as colleagues and campaigns to break price-fixing on books and over-the-counter medicines.
ASDA was also the first supermarket to introduce round-the-clock opening before Christmas in 1995.
Leighton has worked closely with Norman and is expected to maintain a similar style with the company but analysts will also be looking for him to introduce an individual stamp.

"The management team is very strong but under Norman's leadership it was focused on recovering ASDA and opening new store space. Now, under Leighton, it should look to move things forward and we could see some very interesting innovations," the analyst said.
